A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LASER-VFL work and contain readable methods, equations, experiments, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E. Pagination and float placement change, but the material supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original predictive-performance and runtime experiments in Section 5, plus nonuniform-missingness experiments in Appendix E.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and reports revised measurements in Table 1, Figure 2, and Appendix E.

M1.justification: Parameter sharing, representation averaging, weighted task sampling, and Algorithms 1–2 remain substantively unchanged. The corrected summation notation in Equation (7) and Algorithm 1 cross-reference do not change the procedure.

E1.justification: Both evaluate HAPT, Credit, MIMIC-IV mortality prediction, CIFAR-10, and CIFAR-100. Uniform missingness, varying client counts, and nonuniform missingness scenarios are retained without added tasks or populations.

E2.justification: Local, Standard VFL, VFedTrans, Ensemble, Combinatorial, and PlugVFL retain their corresponding comparisons. VFedTrans remains restricted to HAPT and Credit; Figure 2 and Table 3 retain the same comparator sets, including PlugVFL.

E3.justification: Reported settings remain unchanged: four clients and missingness probabilities 0, 0.1, and 0.5 in Table 1; client-count scaling at missingness 0.1 in Figure 2; and Beta(2,2) missingness in Appendix E. Appendix D retains the same model families and metric definitions. Changed scores do not establish an undocumented protocol change.

E4.justification: The existing client-count and nonuniform-missingness analyses receive revised quantitative evidence without new analytical questions or conditions. For example, Table 3 changes LASER-VFL accuracy from 87.3 ± 1.3 to 81.7 ± 1.0 when training and inference missingness probabilities are independently Beta-distributed. No component ablation is added.

E5.justification: Tables 1 and 3 retain averaging over five seeds with standard deviations, and Figure 2 retains uncertainty bands. Revised deviations and the changed statement about being outperformed by more than one standard deviation are result changes, not new statistical procedures.

E6.justification: Table 1 substantially replaces HAPT and CIFAR results; Credit and MIMIC-IV results remain unchanged. At the reported four-client setting with training and inference missingness both 0.5, CIFAR-100 LASER-VFL accuracy changes from 48.7 ± 0.8 to 51.9 ± 1.2, while the strongest baseline shifts from PlugVFL to Ensemble. Figure 2 accuracy curves and Table 3 also change substantially: under nonuniform training and inference missingness, Standard VFL changes from 59.9 ± 12.1 to 13.5 ± 5.3.

T1.justification: Assumptions A1–A4, Lemma 1, both convergence theorems, Appendix C proofs, and Appendix A.2's aggregation argument are retained. Equation renumbering and the observed-client notation correction do not alter mathematical reasoning or guarantees.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: handling arbitrary missing feature blocks efficiently, convergence guarantees, and improved performance even with complete features. The abstract updates numerical illustrations from 18.2% and 7.4% to 19.3% and 9.5%, without changing the scope of these central claims.

C2.justification: Section 5 qualifies Combinatorial's low-missingness advantage from outperforming 'all' baselines to 'most,' specifies when PlugVFL trails Combinatorial or Ensemble, and includes PlugVFL in the explanation of scalability through representation reuse. The task-sampling regularization interpretation and applicability assumptions remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix D retains the same VFedTrans components, PlugVFL adaptation, MIMIC-IV processing description, metric formulas, model families, and runtime information. The code-access statement is unchanged; no new implementation settings or explanation for the revised measurements is supplied.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive positioning against earlier VFL approaches remain unchanged. Valdeira et al. is updated from its 2024 preprint to its 2025 journal publication, representing the same work rather than an added reference.

P1.justification: There are limited rewrites in the experimental discussion, conclusion, and Appendix A.1, along with typo, notation, and cross-reference corrections. A revision date and funding-grant identifier are added. The overall narrative and section structure remain intact.

P2.justification: The figure and table inventory is unchanged. Figure 3 and Table 2 exchange relative placement in the appendices, while Table 3 moves above its explanatory paragraph onto a separate page. Figure 2 retains its plotting structure while displaying revised curves.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly improves clarity and internal consistency by correcting Algorithm 1's loss cross-reference and Equation (7)'s notation, and by replacing the overly broad Combinatorial comparison with a more qualified discussion. The method, theory, evaluation coverage, and reproducibility information remain essentially unchanged. The extensive numerical revisions lack an explanation of their cause, so the larger headline gains alone do not establish a larger quality improvement.
